tests: [click.test] Page.click should click with disabled javascript
[click.test] Page.click should scroll and click with disabled javascript
reason: Turns JavaScript off with page.emulate({ javaScript: "disabled" }), which Firefox refuses Unsupported (emulation.javaScript; Firefox doesn't implement emulation.setScriptingEnabled)

tests: [click.test] Page.click should click with disabled javascript
[click.test] Page.click should scroll and click with disabled javascript
reason: Waits for the same-document navigation a fragment link makes with PageNavigation.next, which stock WebKit's inspector never reports (navigation.sameDocument is unsupported), so the wait would never end. The matrix row doesn't mention the WebKit limit

tests: [click.test] Page.click should not hang with touch-enabled viewports
reason: Emulates a phone: a mobile viewport with touch, which Firefox and stock WebKit refuse Unsupported (emulation.viewport.mobile and emulation.touch)

tests: [click.test] Page.click should click the button with deviceScaleFactor set
reason: A device scale factor other than 1 for the viewport, which stock WebKit refuses Unsupported (emulation.viewport.mobile and its scale); the test also marks clicks with locator.evaluate, which needs isolated worlds

tests: [click.test] Page.click should click the button with fixed position inside an iframe
reason: Styles and marks the frame's button with locator.evaluate, which runs in the isolated world, and stock WebKit has no isolated worlds (isolatedWorlds is unsupported)

Clicks with the back and forward mouse buttons; Strider's Mouse.Button is left, right and middle only, so these buttons have no Strider option. The matrix row says the option is present, which covers only the three buttons
